The Secretary of Defense may acquire real property and carry out the military construction project for the installation outside the United States, and in the amount, set forth in the following table:
Defense Agencies: Outside the United States




CountryLocationAmount
GermanyGemersheim$46,000,000

fable.w: This section only authorizes the Secretary of Defense to acquire real property and carry out a military construction project in Germany at a stated amount. The one tempting reading is that acquiring property abroad implies dealing with outside parties, but the text sets out no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The only actor named is a federal official, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: The Secretary of Defense may acquire real property and carry out the military construction project for the installation outside the United States

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of Defense to acquire property and carry out construction projects. It does not mention any requirement to consult with, coordinate with, or obtain input from parties outside the federal government (such as foreign governments, local communities, or the public) before making these decisions. The text is purely an appropriation/authorization for internal government action.

opus.w: This section only lets the Secretary of Defense buy land and carry out one military construction project in Germany, for a set dollar amount. No party outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue. A foreign location alone does not mean a foreign government takes part in the decision.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that because the project is in Germany, a foreign government must be involved in the decision. That fails because the section never calls for consultation with Germany or anyone else. It only lets the Secretary of Defense buy land and build at one location for a set amount. No comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue is mentioned.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of Defense to acquire property and carry out construction. It does not mention any requirement to consult, coordinate with, or receive input from any party outside the federal government (such as foreign governments, local communities, or advisory boards). The action is purely an internal executive authorization.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that acquiring property "outside the United States" implies coordination with foreign governments, which are outside the federal government. However, the text itself does not explicitly require consultation, coordination, or participation with any foreign entity; it merely authorizes the Secretary to acquire property. Without explicit language mandating interaction with an outside party, this is an internal executive action.
